research_findings: Discovered that waitlist endpoints and public actions lacked rate limiting in the Next.js serverless architecture.

Researched Upstash Redis vs In-Memory solutions. Selected a lightweight in-memory Map rate limiter for Next.js API routes that runs efficiently in edge environments and includes a cleanup interval to prevent memory leaks.
features_improved: Waitlist feature (src/app/actions/waitlist.ts) now has rate limiting based on IP address to prevent abuse and heavy traffic.
Fixed 'Cannot access refs during render' React linter error in AdaptiveCoachDemo component.
new_features_added: In-memory generic rate limiter utility (src/lib/rate-limit.ts) added for immediate protection without external dependencies.
next_steps_for_next_run: Evaluate Upstash Redis integration if traffic exceeds what in-memory limits can handle.
Apply the new rate limiter to other public facing endpoints like signup and password reset.
